Subject: Urgent: Embeds p99 spike after your catalog release

Connor / Laura —

We noticed a sharp regression in embeddings latency starting ~08:45 PDT after the model catalog release you rolled out. Our p95 stayed roughly the same but p99 jumped from ~140ms to ~2.1s for the /v1/embeddings endpoint. This is impacting several downstream pipelines (similarity search and nightly ingestion jobs are timing out).

Quick facts from our side:
- Region: us-west-2
- Endpoint: api.redwood.ai/v1/embeds
- Observed p99: ~2100ms (previously ~120-160ms)
- Error rate increased marginally (0.3% -> 1.6%) when throughput > 120rps

We rolled one of our clients to a cached bucket as a temporary mitigation but need Redwood support to revert or provide a hotfix. Please advise on rollback or immediate mitigations — this needs an exec-level update; our CTO is CC'd.

Attached are a few request traces and stack dumps.

Thanks,
Sanjay
Sanjay Mehta
Head of ML Infrastructure, Acme Analytics

Subject: Re: Urgent: Embeds p99 spike after your catalog release

Connor / team —

We're looking at the rollout logs now. Preliminary findings: during the catalog release at 08:34 PDT we changed the default embeddings variant for a subset of customers to "embed-compact-q4" (smaller quantized variant). That model has a slower cold-start path on our multi-tenant hosted pools because it requires additional per-instance kernel warmups and a slightly different memory layout that bypasses our small-batch fast-path. For typical batch sizes (1-8 vectors) that added ~1.8s at the p99 tail on a handful of nodes before they were warmed.

Short-term mitigations we can do immediately:
1) Roll back the default model for Acme to the previous "embed-stable-v1" variant (we can pin per-account) — ETA: 15m to take effect (routing propagation + warm pools).
2) Adjust routing so Acme traffic is steered to nodes with warm kernels (we can force a warmup by sending synthetic low-cost requests).
3) For hosted customers hitting higher throughput, enable eager model warmup for new variants by default (one-off config) — this reduces the cold-start tail but increases infra usage during rollout.

I'm triggering (1) now for Acme across us-west-2 and us-east-1. Will report once propagation completes and we have updated p99 metrics.

Marcus Lin
VP, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-03-27T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Actioned: routing + warmup + temporary rate shape applied

Sanjay / Connor —

Update from SRE: we've completed the following actions as of 12:28 PDT: 
- Rolled Acme back to embed-stable-v1 (per-account pin) in us-west-2 and us-east-1.
- Forced warmup on 10 nodes serving Acme by replaying low-cost init requests; kernel warm paths are now hot.
- Enabled a temporary rate-shaping rule to smooth bursts > 100rps (helps avoid queue amplification that pushed p99 up).
- Increased autoscaler aggressiveness for embeddings pools for the next 3 hours to handle potential bursts.

Preliminary metrics: p95 unchanged, p99 reduced from ~2100ms to ~180ms on the affected thundering subset. We'll continue to monitor over the next 2 hours and push a small infra change to avoid the slow cold path for compact quant variants.

Attachments: latency_report_acme_20260327.pdf, embed_node_logs_03-27.zip

Hannah Schmitt
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Executive summary & next steps — embeddings p99 regression (Acme)

Tara / Sanjay —

Thanks again for raising this. Below is a concise summary for your exec team and ours. Happy to jump on a call to walk through details.

What happened:
- On 2026-03-27 at ~08:34 PDT a catalog change promoted a quantized compact embeddings variant (embed-compact-q4) as the default for a subset of hosted customers. The variant introduced an unexpected cold-path kernel warmup that increased p99 on small-batch traffic.

Impact:
- Acme observed p99 spikes from ~120ms to ~2.1s for the /v1/embeddings endpoint between 08:45–12:20 PDT, affecting similarity queries and batch ingestion. Error rates rose slightly at >120rps.

Immediate remediation (completed):
- Per-account pin to embed-stable-v1 for Acme (12:28 PDT).
- Forced node warmups and temporary rate-shaping.
- Autoscaler tuning to mitigate queueing at burst points.

Ongoing fixes (next 7 days):
- Runtime team will add an eager warmup during catalog rollouts for quantized variants to eliminate cold-path tail (owner: Marcus).
- SRE will add a rollout safety gate to avoid auto-promotion of variants without a warm-path check (owner: Hannah).
- Product will update catalog release notes and add a per-account opt-out switch for auto-migration (owner: Marissa).

Customer asks we are actioning:
- Exec write-up and postmortem (we will deliver within 48 hours).
- Goodwill credit review (Connor & Laura to follow up on commercial terms).
- A technical follow-up call with runtime & SRE to go over warmup plan (scheduled by Marissa).

Next steps / timeline:
- 48h: postmortem & mitigations plan delivered.
- 7d: deploy warmup and rollout safety gate (can be staged).
- Commercial: Connor/Laura to propose credit and contractual remedies by EOD 2026-03-30.

If you'd like a call now, we can be available this afternoon.

Regards,
